title: Block B close: prophets and light
hook: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Musa, Yusuf, Maryam, Ayyub, Yunus, all in one arc
carry: they all said the same one thing

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ledger turned to good, and your line was turned to good. What small opposite did you do? Day five hundred one, the last day of Block B.

Seventy-two days ago, on day four hundred twenty-nine, Block B opened with Surah Yunus. Since then the path has walked through sixteen surahs, from Yunus to Al-Furqan, and they've been crowded with people. A man building a ship on dry land while his neighbors laughed. Two prophets warning two vanished peoples. A boy thrown into a well who grew up to forgive his brothers. A man who saw a fire in the desert and walked toward it. A young mother under a palm tree. A sick man who named his pain. A prophet calling out from the dark inside a whale. Different centuries, different places. And yet.
screen: `A SHIP ON DRY LAND, A BOY IN A WELL.`

segments.voice: Here's Block B in a handful of doors. Yunus and Hud: Nuh and his ark, Hud and Salih sent to 'Ad and Thamud, and the friends of God who neither fear nor grieve. Yusuf: the well, the prison, and no blame on you today. Ar-Ra'd and Ibrahim: the thunder glorifying, and a good word like a good tree. Al-Isra and Al-Kahf: the night journey, the young men in the cave, and the stranger who explained what Musa couldn't bear. Maryam and Ta-Ha: the palm tree in labor, the fire Musa walked toward, and 'ilm, increase me in knowledge. Al-Anbiya: Ayyub, Zakariyya, and rahmatan lil-'alamin. Al-Hajj, Al-Mu'minun, An-Nur, Al-Furqan: the pilgrims' call, the believers, mishkat, and the servants of the Merciful who walk gently. Now listen for the line that keeps coming back. Surah Hud tells the stories of Nuh, Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb, and each of them opens with nearly the same words to his people: worship God; you have no god but Him. Al-Anbiya says it outright: God sent no messenger before Muhammad ﷺ without revealing to him that there is no god but God, so worship Him. That's the arc of this whole block. The Qur'an doesn't present these prophets as founders of different faiths. It presents them as one long line of messengers, each sent to their own people in their own language, each saying the same one thing. Different storms, different deserts, different kings. One message. And between the stories, light: on a lamp in a niche, on a pilgrim's road, on a heart that sees.
screen: `NUH, HUD, SALIH; THE FRIENDS OF GOD.` · `YUSUF; THE CAVE; THE PALM; THE FIRE.` · `AYYUB; LIGHT UPON LIGHT.` · `ONE LINE OF MESSENGERS, ONE MESSAGE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: name a prophet you feel close to. Sit, and breathe. Let the faces of this block pass by slowly: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Yusuf, Musa, Maryam, Zakariyya, Ayyub, Yunus. Notice which one you stay with. The one in the well, maybe, or the one in the dark, or the one asking not to be left alone. Ask yourself why that one. When the bell ends, write down the name and one sentence about why. If you pray, you can send peace on them. The bell holds the time.
Rasul, a messenger: the word for every prophet from Yunus to Al-Furqan, one long line of messengers sent with the same message. Today's word.

Your line: they all said the same one thing. Tomorrow, the path steps into the Islamic year itself, its holy days and months, starting with Muharram. Today, keep your prophet's name with you. Day five hundred one.

howItsDone: Muslims believe in all the prophets the Qur'an names, from Adam to Muhammad, as one line of messengers bringing the same core message of God's oneness, and add 'peace be upon him' after each name.

original.note: Arabic: rasul, a messenger; the Qur'an speaks of messengers sent to every people.

trapdoor: what you thought: a block of stories about different prophets.
what it means: one long line of messengers, each sent to their own people, each with the same message: there is no god but God.
what a scholar hears: the recurring formula 'ya qawmi 'budu llaha ma lakum min ilahin ghayruh' (11:50, 11:61, 11:84); 21:25 states the principle; 14:4 says each messenger spoke his people's language.

notes: No direct quotations; 21:25 and the Hud formula are paraphrased.

Block B covered surahs 10–25 (sixteen surahs) over days 429–501 (seventy-three days); the 'doors' list summarizes themes from the outline. Confirm each item matches what earlier days actually taught (e.g. Al-Hijr and An-Nahl are folded into the list only implicitly).
